guide.whenCaution: Not every NPC, monster or situation is a threat. If it won't get worse when left alone, it is just a danger to be faced. Don't write one up unless you know it is going to be a big deal.
guide.typeMoves: What a threat of this type does next

burnBrightly.title: Burn Brightly
burnBrightly.description: When you have enough XP to Level Up (6 + twice your current level), you may spend 2 XP after any roll you make to add +1 to that roll (max +1 per roll).
burnBrightly.promptNote: When you meet the requirements, you'll be prompted in chat after a roll.
burnBrightly.tooltip: When you have enough XP to Level Up, you may spend 2 XP after any roll you make to add +1 to that roll (max +1 per roll).
burnBrightly.drivenTooltip: Driven: you always have the option to Burn Brightly; you can spend 2 XP after you roll to add +1 (max +1 per roll), even if you don't have enough XP to level.
burnBrightly.notEnoughXp: You don't have enough XP to Burn Brightly.
burnBrightly.notYours: Only the player of the character who made this roll can Burn Brightly on it.
burnBrightly.zeroHp: Burn Brightly cannot change a roll made at 0 HP from the card: its result is already settled.

deathsDoor.title: Death's Door
deathsDoor.clear: No longer out of the action
deathsDoor.clearFateHint: Takes the sheet off "a fate is owed" without choosing one, for a table who played the 6- out in conversation, or took the roll back. Until this is cleared the character is never recognised as dying again.
deathsDoor.fatePendingHint: You rolled a 6-. Your time has come. Choose how it ends.
deathsDoor.supersededHint: You've already died once. At 0 HP you trigger {move} instead. It's on your Moves tab.
deathsDoor.outOfActionHint: No longer dying, but out of the action until the GM says otherwise.
deathsDoor.dispersedHint: Your essence has dispersed. You reform near your tether at the next sunset with {hp} HP.
deathsDoor.backOnFeetHint: Out of the action. Back on your feet, you return with {hp} HP.
deathsDoor.deadHint: They stepped through the Last Door.
deathsDoor.monsterHint: Their tenuous connection to humanity is lost: they became a monster under the GM's control.
deathsDoor.threatHint: Their humanity is utterly lost: they became a threat in the GM's control.
deathsDoor.undeathNotDying: {move} is {name}'s move at 0 HP, and {name} is not dying.
deathsDoor.postDeathTabHint: Opens the Post-Death tab, where you can take the Revenant, Ghost or Thrall insert. Death's Door grants one for you on a 6-. Use this if your table resolved that away from the sheet.
deathsDoor.lockedHint: Only available when the character is dying: at 0 HP, with the move still to face.
deathsDoor.claimHeld: {name} is already rolling Death's Door for {actor}, so nothing was rolled here. This window follows their roll.
deathsDoor.claimSettled: Death's Door for {actor} was settled before this roll could start, so nothing was rolled.
deathsDoor.privateBoostsNeedGM: This roll was private, so Burn Brightly and giving it your all need the GM online to change its card.
deathsDoor.boostRelayFailed: The GM's client couldn't change the roll's card. Try again, or accept the result as it stands.
deathsDoor.yieldTaken: {name} took over Death's Door for {actor}, so this window lands nothing.
deathsDoor.yieldSettled: Death's Door for {actor} was settled from another window, so this one lands nothing.

tiers.success: You wrest yourself back to the realm of the living—return to 1 HP but say how your brush with death has marked you.
tiers.partial: The Lady waves you off—you’re no longer dying but you’re out of the action.

lastDoor.label: Make one last move as if you rolled a 12+, then step through the Last Door
lastDoor.hint: After that they're dead. There's no saving them, and that last move can't be used to avoid death.

refuse.label: Refuse to go; gain the Revenant or Ghost insert
refuse.hint: The GM will ask why. If you can't say what you refuse to leave undone, your Terrible Purpose, you shouldn't pick this.

thrall.label: Call on one of the Things Below by name and beseech it to intercede; gain the Thrall insert
thrall.hint: You must know the name of a Thing Below. If none have come up in play, you can't call on one.

refusalHints.revenant: You cling stubbornly to your body.
refusalHints.ghost: Your body is dead and gone; your soul lingers.

refused.intro: You refused to go, and the Last Door let you back. Here is what that costs.
refused.card: {who} refuses the Last Door and gains the {what} insert.
refused.next: Choose your Terrible Purpose and your first Consequence.

undying.intro: You gave up the body you clung to, and your spirit lingers on. Your Terrible Purpose stays with you; as a Ghost, you choose a first Consequence of your own.

thrall.intro: You called one of the Things Below by name, and it answered. Here is what that costs.
thrall.card: {who} calls on a Thing Below by name, and it intercedes: gaining the {what} insert.
thrall.next: Name your master; your GM will choose the Mark it leaves on you.

mark.spectator: The mark it left is on the sheet: {name} says how it marked them.
mark.seedFailed: Couldn't record the Death's-Door mark: describe it and it will try again.

orphaned.stale: {name} started it over {minutes} minutes ago and hasn't finished it.

notes.skipped: {move}: you didn't roll, and you get a {tier}.

roll.describe: The Lady of Crows and the Last Door are yours and your table's to describe. They might even appear differently for different characters.
roll.destined: {name}: until your destiny is fulfilled, a 6- counts as a 7-9, and a 7-9 as a 10+.
roll.neverGonna: {name}: once per session, when you are at Death's Door, don't roll. You get a 10+.
roll.neverGonnaUsed: {name}: already used this session, so this time you roll.
roll.noRush: No rush: the book lets you hold off until the scene wraps up or the other PCs get a little spotlight. "Not yet" closes this and leaves you dying.

watch.rolled: They rolled {total}, and it hasn't landed yet: they can still accept it or push it up.
watch.inTheAir: The dice are still in the air.
watch.takeOverAccepts: Taking it over doesn't roll again: you get the result they rolled, to accept.
watch.takeOverRolls: Nothing of it reached the table, so taking it over lets you roll it yourself.
watch.follows: This window follows their roll, and shows the result when it lands.

result.burnOffer: Burn Brightly: spend {cost} XP to add +1 to the roll.
result.giveAllOffer: Impetuous Youth: give it your all to turn it into the next result up, and pick what it costs you.
result.orAccept: Or accept it as it stands.
result.restored: Back to 1 HP, and no longer dying.
result.outOfAction: No longer dying. Unconscious, or close enough, until the GM says otherwise, still at 0 HP.
result.debilityTraded: Debility marked: you regain 1 HP and stay on your feet.
result.debilityAsk: Hard to Kill — mark a debility of your choice to regain 1 HP:

result.fateSpectator: The fate is {name}'s to choose. If they have left, close this and open Death's Door again from the sheet to choose it for them.
result.fateRecorded: Your fate is recorded. The GM will take it from here.

fate.title: Refuse to Go
fate.intro: The GM will ask why you refuse. Name the person, the task, or the reckoning you will not leave behind. That's your Terrible Purpose. Then say which way you stay.

choices.railLabel: What the {name} insert asks of you
choices.noRush: No rush: whatever you leave undecided is waiting on your Post-Death tab, and can be answered there in edit mode.

chat.skipped: {name} doesn't roll Death's Door, and gets a 10+.
chat.skippedRule: Once per session, when you are at Death's Door, don't roll. You get a 10+.
chat.unstoppableOne: {name} survives, and clears their Unstoppable circle.
chat.unstoppableMany: {name} survives, and clears all {count} Unstoppable circles.
chat.lastDoor: {name} makes one last move as if they rolled a 12+, then steps through the Last Door.
chat.lastDoorRule: There's no saving them. Only the rarest of magic can bring them back.

buttons.burnTitle: Burn Brightly: spend {cost} XP after you roll to add +1 (max +1 per roll)
buttons.giveAllTitle: Impetuous Youth: turn a 6- into a 7-9, or a 7-9 into a 10+. Pick 1: you get hurt (2d4 damage and an actual injury); you escalate the situation; or something on your person is lost or breaks.

deathsDoor.summary: When you are dying, you glimpse the Last Door and the Lady of Crows. Roll +nothing: on a 10+ return to 1 HP; on a 7-9 you're out of action; on a 6- choose a dark fate.
deathsDoor.description: When you are dying, you glimpse the Last Door and the Lady of Crows (describe it). Then, roll +nothing: on a 10+, you wrest yourself back to the realm of the living—return to 1 HP but say how your brush with death has marked you; on a 7-9, the Lady waves you off—you're no longer dying but you're out of the action; on a 6-, your time has come—choose 1: make one last move as if you rolled a 12+, then step through the Last Door; refuse to go and gain the Revenant or Ghost insert; or call on one of the Things Below by name and beseech it to intercede, gaining the Thrall insert.

levelUp.title: Level Up
levelUp.summary: When you have a quiet stretch of time at home and enough XP, walk through the steps to level up your character.
levelUp.description: When you have a quiet stretch of time at home and XP equal to (or greater than) 6 + twice your current level, follow the Level Up steps.
levelUp.lockedHint: Requires XP equal to or greater than 6 + twice your current level.
levelUp.overviewIntro: When you have a quiet stretch of time at home and XP equal to (or greater than) 6 + twice your current level, you're ready to level up.
levelUp.invocationAside: Your new level is even, so you'll also choose a new Invocation on the next step.
levelUp.moveIntro: Choose one new move from your playbook.
levelUp.noMoves: No additional moves are available at this level.
levelUp.invocationIntro: Choose one new Invocation to add to your repertoire.
levelUp.statIntro: Choose which stat to raise by +1.
levelUp.statAllAtCap: All of your stats are already at this move's maximum. Go back and pick a different move.
levelUp.foreignIntro: Choose the move this grants you from another playbook (you must qualify for it):
levelUp.foreignEmpty: You don't currently qualify for any move from the allowed playbooks. Continue to finish.
levelUp.marksIntro: Make this move's selection(s) for the level you're gaining.
levelUp.markFromBackground: From your Background: you already have this one.
levelUp.companionIntro: Beast-Bonded: mark another action you can use when you focus on your animal companion.
levelUp.reviewReminder: Last, review your Instinct and Appearance on the Details tab. Change anything that no longer applies, or make up something new.
levelUp.again: You have enough XP to level up again, so here's the next one.
levelUp.refusedLevel: This level-up was already applied, so nothing changed. Open Level Up again if there's another level to take.
levelUp.refusedXp: Not enough XP to level up any more, so nothing changed. Levelling up costs 6 + twice your current level.

outfit.title: Outfit
outfit.description: When you prepare for an expedition in a friendly community, mark as many ◊ on your Inventory insert as you wish to carry, either on specific items or in "undefined." Mark up to 3 ◊ for a light load (quick and quiet), 4-6 ◊ for a normal load, or 7-9 ◊ for a heavy load (noisy, slow, quick to tire). Also, mark a number of □ in the Small items section equal to 4+Prosperity (on specific items or "undefined").
outfit.selectPrinted: Items printed on the Inventory insert
outfit.selectTrade: Special items for which you Trade & Barter
outfit.tellGm: Tell the GM what you're bringing, and answer their questions about your gear and where you got it.
outfit.loadHeavy: Heavy load: noisy, slow, quick to tire
outfit.loadBonusNote: With {moves}, every load allows {bonus} more ◆: up to {light} light, {normal} normal, {heavy} heavy.

recover.title: Recover
recover.summary: When you take time to catch your breath and tend to what ails you, expend 1 use of supplies and regain HP equal to 4+Prosperity. The same move also tends a debility or a problematic wound (use the wound's Tend button); the GM says it's handled or names what's still required.
recover.lockedHint: You've already caught your breath — you can't gain this benefit again until you take more damage.
recover.noSuppliesHint: You have no uses of supplies to expend.
recover.unlivingHint: Unliving: no benefit. A Ghost or Revenant gains nothing from Recover.

convalesce.title: Convalesce
convalesce.summary: When you rest for a few days, in safety and comfort, recover all your HP and clear all your debilities.
convalesce.nothingHint: You're already at full HP with no debilities to clear.
convalesce.unlivingHint: Unliving: no benefit. A Ghost or Revenant gains nothing from Convalesce.

specialMoves.dyingHint: Dying: you can't save yourself. Someone who tends you Aids your {move} roll instead.

undeath.becameGhost: Gave up the Revenant insert and became a Ghost. Your Terrible Purpose stays with you; choose your first Consequence as a Ghost.
undeath.ghostDown: Your body is given up, so no HP comes back now: you're out of the action until you reform (Reform at your tether, on your Special Moves tab).
undeath.taskStanding: Your master's task still stands: "{task}". A new task takes its place.

unholyVessel.label: Unholy Vessel
unholyVessel.warning: You would gain a Mark, but there are none left to gain. Your humanity is utterly lost: you become a threat in the GM's control. Make a new character.
unholyVessel.summary: Unholy Vessel: there is no Mark left to gain. {name}'s humanity is utterly lost, and they become a threat in the GM's control. Make a new character.

postDeath.chooseFateHint: You take one of these only when it becomes relevant: you died, and refused to go. Death's Door grants it for you on a 6-; pick one here if your table resolved that away from the sheet.
postDeath.hideTabHint: Take this tab off the sheet. It comes back on its own if this character takes an insert, or faces the Last Door.
postDeath.tetherHint: Tethered reforms you beside it. If it's ever destroyed, you mark the Final Consequence.
postDeath.tetherPlaceholder: Your mortal remains, the place where you died, an object of significance…
postDeath.tetherMissing: Name your tether. Tethered can't resolve without knowing where you reform.
postDeath.crossedOffHint: Dark Succor took these away. You can never gain them.
postDeath.masterTaskHint: Until it's done, your Favor stays at 0.
postDeath.retiredTooltip: Who they were before they died. The playbook and its Instinct are still on the sheet, and come back if the insert is removed.
postDeath.instinctRetired: Retired when you took the insert. It comes back if the insert is removed.
postDeath.deadTooltip: They made one last move as if they rolled a 12+, then stepped through the Last Door. Only the rarest of magic can bring them back.
postDeath.deadTooltipAction: They made one last move as if they rolled a 12+, then stepped through the Last Door. Only the rarest of magic can bring them back. Click here if it has.
postDeath.raiseHpNote: Their hit points have just gone above 0.
postDeath.raiseAsk: Only the rarest of magic can bring them back. Is that what happened?
postDeath.raised: {name} is no longer dead. Their sheet is their own again.
postDeath.raiseFailed: Couldn't clear the dead state. Try again, or clear it on the Special Moves tab.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
outcomes.hint: The triggers happen in the fiction. When one does, press what it earned you: your Purpose's own words say which of these, and whether it is one or two.
outcomes.indulge: Indulged: advantage on your next roll
outcomes.reasonNoConsequence: No consequence is marked that can be cleared.
outcomes.reasonNoneLeft: Every consequence you could take is already marked.
outcomes.clearConsequenceAsk: Which consequence is cleared? The Final Consequence is never one of them.
outcomes.lastDoorBody: {name}'s Terrible Purpose ({source}) is at its end. They pass through the Last Door and leave play. Only the rarest of magic can bring them back.
outcomes.rolledNoGain: rolled {roll}, but they are already at full HP.
outcomes.indulged: Indulged their Strange Appetites: advantage on their next roll.
outcomes.favorHeldByTask: Held at 0 until your master's task is done
outcomes.favorCautionTask: Your master's task isn't done yet, and until it is, your Favor stays at 0 (Dark Succor).
outcomes.favorHint: A ticked pip is Favor held. Click a pip to set your Favor to it.
outcomes.gainMarkHint: When Favor goes past 3 and you choose a new Mark: your Favor goes to 0. Then the GM crosses off one you don't have. With none left to gain, it is Unholy Vessel.
outcomes.crossOffLabel: Cross off {name}: this Thrall can never gain it
outcomes.uncrossLabel: Restore {name}: it was crossed off by mistake
outcomes.taskBody: Is {task} done? Clearing it lets your Favor rise again.
outcomes.taskDoneLine: Completed the master's task: {task}. Favor can rise again.
outcomes.cautionNeedsFirst: {name} requires {requires}, which is not marked. Flagged, not blocked.
outcomes.cautionTwoPurposes: The Terrible Purpose is choose 1, but {names} are marked together. Flagged, not blocked.
outcomes.finalBody: The Final Consequence ends {name} as a player character: their tenuous connection to humanity is lost, and they become a monster under the GM's control.
outcomes.finalYes: Mark it: they become a monster
outcomes.finalUndoBody: Unmarking the Final Consequence brings {name} back into play as a player character, with the hit points they have now.

arcana.createGmOnly: Only the GM can create homebrew arcana in this world.

arcana.identifyAdvantage: This falls under one of the moves below, so roll with advantage.
arcana.giveCardHint: Hand this arcanum to the player without a roll.

arcana.backOwedText: You've read the front. The back is owed you, once you've had time to study it or learn more.
arcana.unidentifiedText: This arcanum has not yet been identified. You can tell it's something, but not what.
arcana.discoverConfirm: Have you tracked down and recovered this arcanum? Its full details will be revealed.
arcana.leadText: You have a lead on this arcanum's whereabouts, but haven't recovered it yet.
arcana.missingText: This arcanum's card can no longer be found in this world. Remove it to clear its marks.

inventory.smallItemsNote:
Fit in a pocket, pouch, or boot.
When you Outfit, mark □ below equal to 4+Prosperity.
inventory.smallItemsNoteWithLimit:
Fit in a pocket, pouch, or boot.

inventory.worldCreated: Created inventory item "{name}". Drag it onto a character's Inventory tab to add it.
inventory.dropAddedUnlinked: Added {names} to {actor}'s character sheet. This token isn't linked to {actor}, so anything dropped on it would otherwise have stayed on the token and never reached the player.
inventory.addItemColumnHint: Which inventory column this item lands in when dropped. An immobile thing lists with the small items and carries the immobile tag, as the book prints it.
inventory.addItemWeightHint: ◇ counts toward your load. Armor subtracts from damage you take (worn items only).
inventory.addItemArmorWornHint: Tick for body armor (mail, hides, a cuirass): the best worn armor counts, they don't stack. Leave clear for a shield or a bonus, which adds on top.
inventory.addItemTagsHint: Shown in parentheses after the name. Click a tag to add it, or type your own.
inventory.addItemUsesHint: How many ○ circles to track. Tick "Ammunition" for a bow/crossbow's low-ammo / all-out track.
inventory.addItemUsesLabelsHint: One line per circle, printed after it. Leave a line blank to skip a circle, e.g. four blank lines then "out" to mark only the fifth. Ignored while Ammunition is ticked.
inventory.addItemResourceFirst: Print the track before the tags
inventory.addItemResourceFirstHint: As the book prints the bullseye lantern: "○○○○○ Oil, near" rather than "near ○○○○○ Oil".
inventory.addItemShield: Shield (+1 Readiness on a 7+ to Defend)
inventory.addItemValueHint: What it's worth in trade, printed at the end of its tags ("Value 3"). Leave blank if it has none.
inventory.treasureCreated: Created treasure "{name}". Only the GM can see it until you drag it onto a character's Inventory tab.
inventory.treasureLoreHint: What it looks like, what it truly does, and any custom move's full text. The player reads it once they've identified it (a 10+ to Know Things).
inventory.treasureStartsHiddenHint: The player sees only its name and ◇ until they work it out. Leave clear to follow the world setting "Artifacts Arrive Unidentified".
inventory.resetConfirm: Clear all item marks and the undefined ◇/□ pools? Item uses (e.g. supplies) are not affected.
inventory.regularUndefinedPoolNote: Click to reserve undefined ◆. When you Have What You Need, mark an item below. It draws from here.
inventory.smallUndefinedPoolNote: Click to reserve undefined ■. When you Have What You Need, mark a small item below. It draws from here.
inventory.regularPoolAtLimit: You're already carrying a full load, so there's no room to reserve more undefined ◇. Un-mark a carried item to free up room.
inventory.smallPoolAtLimit: You've used all your small-item slots, so there's no room to reserve more undefined □. Un-mark a small item to free up room.
inventory.smallOverAllotment: That's more small items than your Outfit allotment of {limit} (4+Prosperity). Expend a use of supplies to carry an extra small item, or check with your GM.
inventory.possessionsOverLimitOne: This character has 1 more special possession than the playbook lets you choose.
inventory.possessionsOverLimitMany: This character has {count} more special possessions than the playbook lets you choose.
inventory.possessionsOverLimitHint: Turn on Edit and untick one, or leave it if your GM agreed to it.

outfit.heavy: For a heavy load (noisy, slow, hot, quick to tire), mark {band} ◆

attackFx.name: Attack Effects on the Map
attackFx.hint: When on, a blow that lands is drawn on the map and heard at the table: a sword swings, an arrow flies, a thrown spear arcs, a bite snaps on the one bitten. A ranged miss flies wide, and pressing Apply bursts on every token that loses HP, or clanks when armor held. The pictures need the Sequencer and JB2A modules, and the sounds need the SoundFx Library module; without them, that half does nothing. Anyone whose system asks for reduced motion, who has switched Sequencer's Enable Effects off, or who has switched Foundry's Photosensitive Mode on, keeps the sounds without the pictures.

weatherSceneFx.name: Weather on the Scene (FXMaster)
weatherSceneFx.hint: When on, posting a result from the Weather window puts the matching particles on the scene your players are on: rain for rain, snow for snow, racing cloud for a storm, and a clear sky for the fine days. Requires the FXMaster module (FXMaster+ counts); without it this does nothing. Only the effects this system adds are ever touched, so any you set up yourself stay put. The Weather window carries this same switch as a Pause button, which also takes whatever is falling right now off the map.

weatherFxClouds.name: Weather Effects: Cloud
weatherFxClouds.hint: Drifting cloud, which most of the skies wear: a few for a fine day, a low lid for an overcast one, and a dark ceiling racing over for the storms. Off leaves the fine, overcast and windy days with nothing on the map at all, since cloud is all they draw.

weatherFxFog.name: Weather Effects: Fog
weatherFxFog.hint: The low haze that sits over the ground on a muggy day. The only sky that draws it.

weatherFxRain.name: Weather Effects: Rain
weatherFxRain.hint: Falling rain, from a shower to a downpour to the driven rain of a storm or a tornado. The cloud above it is a separate switch.

weatherFxHail.name: Weather Effects: Hail
weatherFxHail.hint: Hail, which only a storm throws, mixed in with its rain.

weatherFxSnowstorm.name: Weather Effects: Blizzard Snow
weatherFxSnowstorm.hint: The driven snow of a blizzard, which is a heavier effect than ordinary snow and switches separately from it.

weatherFxStormTint.name: Weather Effects: Storm Light
weatherFxStormTint.hint: The slate grey a storm or a tornado washes the daylight with. Off keeps the cloud and the rain and leaves your map its own colours.

alwaysShowMapPinNames.name: Map Pin Names: Show By Default
alwaysShowMapPinNames.hint: When on (the default), a Stonetop map pin wears its name on the map instead of waiting for the cursor. The poster maps are the unlabelled printing of artwork the books print labelled, and this puts the names back. Covers the lettered places of interest, the regional and village map markers, and your threat, hazard and site pins. This is the default every map follows unless you give it an answer of its own below, and it is the only answer for scenes that are not poster maps.

mapPinNameSettings.name: Map Pin Names
mapPinNameSettings.label: Configure
mapPinNameSettings.hint: Choose whether Stonetop map pins wear their names on the map, for all maps at once or one poster map at a time.
mapPinNameSettings.title: Map Pin Names
mapPinNameSettings.perMapNote: Each imported poster map can answer for itself. A map set to follow the world setting changes with it; one given an answer of its own keeps that answer whatever the setting above says.

customMovesGmOnly.name: Custom Moves: GM Only
customMovesGmOnly.hint: When on, only the GM can create or edit custom moves. Players don't see the "+ Custom Move" button or the edit pencils. Existing custom moves still display and roll for everyone. Turn off to let players author their own custom moves (including ongoing bonuses).

arcanaCreationGmOnly.name: Arcana Creation: GM Only
arcanaCreationGmOnly.hint: When on, only the GM can create homebrew arcana. Players don't see the "Create major/minor arcanum" buttons on the arcana tab. Existing arcana still display, flip, and roll for everyone, and players can still edit cards they own. Turn off to let players author their own arcana.

monsterBuilderEnabled.name: Guided Monster Builder
monsterBuilderEnabled.hint: When on (the default), creating a blank Monster from "Create Actor" opens a guided worksheet (Book I, "Dangers") that walks you through the book's steps and computes HP, Armor, and Damage from your tag picks. Turn off to create a blank stat block instead. Compendium imports, drag-drops, and duplicates are never intercepted.

showRelationshipMap.name: Relationship Map
showRelationshipMap.hint: When on (the default), the table shares a relationship map: a tab on the steading sheet, a button in the Journal tab and a hotbar macro. Turn it off to take all three away for everyone. Nothing drawn on the map is lost, and it comes back as it was when you turn it on again.

showTimeline.name: Timeline
showTimeline.hint: When on (the default), the steading and every character have a Timeline tab, and the Chronicle folder holds the Timeline journal. Turn it off to take the tabs and the journal away for everyone. It goes on recording in the background while it is off, so nothing is missing when you turn it on again.

arcanaPlayersSeeBothSides.name: Arcana: Players See Both Sides
arcanaPlayersSeeBothSides.hint: A player always sees the back of a card once they've unlocked it (filled every spot). That's their own achievement, no setting needed. This switch is a separate peek: when on, players may also open the back of a card they haven't unlocked yet, reading the whole card up front. Off by default for a more secretive table: an un-unlocked back stays hidden until you click "Reveal back to player" on that card (handy when a card must be read before it can be unlocked). Turn on to let players read cards up front. You always see both sides as the GM.

threatOnCanvasCards.name: Threats: Show Cards on the Map
threatOnCanvasCards.hint: When on, a threat pinned to a scene also draws its full card on the map, anchored to the pin and moving with the scene, so you can read it and tick off its doom track right there on the canvas. Off by default: the pin opens the same card in a window instead. Threats are GM-only prep, so these pins and cards are only ever shown to you.

sheetFontScale.name: Sheet Font Size
sheetFontScale.hint: Scale the text on Stonetop sheets, dialogs and chat cards to make it easier to read. 1.00 is the size the sheets were drawn at, so 1.25 is a quarter larger again and 1.40 is the largest.

sheetContrast.name: Dark Mode
sheetContrast.hint: The page behind Stonetop sheets, dialogs and chat cards. Dark (Lamplit) is light ink on a warm, dark page, easier on the eyes at night and for readers bothered by glare. Dark (Slate) is the same in a cool blue-grey. Follow Foundry uses Lamplit whenever Foundry's own theme is dark, and parchment when it is light. Tick High Contrast below to go with any of them. None of these touch the paper grain, so set that below to taste.

highContrast.name: High Contrast
highContrast.hint: Darken every grey and coloured text well past the readability guideline, on plain white paper, or on a darker page in Dark Mode. Adds a clearer focus ring, underlined links and heavier dividing lines. Pair it with a larger font size above.

mapBrightness.name: Map Brightness
mapBrightness.hint: Dim the imported Stonetop maps (The Village, The Vicinity, World's End, Marshedge and Gordin's Delve), as scenes, in the Setting Overview pages, and on an expedition's route map. 100 is as imported; lower takes the glare off, which helps most in Dark Mode. Only on this computer. Other maps, and the rulebook pages, are left alone.

sheetTexture.name: Paper Texture
sheetTexture.hint: Show the faint grain on the paper behind Stonetop sheets, dialogs and chat cards. Turn it off for a flat page, which is easier to read text on. This works on its own, whatever Dark Mode and High Contrast are set to.

sheetTextureFade.name: Paper Texture Transparency
sheetTextureFade.hint: How faint the spirals and grain on the paper are, while Paper Texture is on. 0 shows them at full strength; higher fades them further into the page, up to 90. 30 is the default.

noItalics.name: No Italic Text
noItalics.hint: Draw every slanted word upright instead, everywhere in Foundry rather than only on Stonetop sheets. Italic text is harder to read, especially under a magnifier. The trade is that italics are how some things mark themselves out (a move's fiction, the hint under a field, a note saying a list is empty), so those will read the same as the text around them once this is on.

worldSheetLayout.name: Sheet Layout (Whole Table)
worldSheetLayout.hint: Which sheet layout this world uses for everyone who has not chosen their own below. Modern puts the tabs on an icon strip down the outside of the window and moves the stats block onto a tab; Classic is the older look, with a row of tab names across the top of the sheet and the stats block always on screen above them. New worlds start on Modern; a world that already existed before the two layouts were added stays on Classic until you change it here. Monster sheets have no tabs and look the same either way.

sheetLayout.name: Sheet Layout (Just for Me)
sheetLayout.hint: Overrides the table-wide layout on this browser only, so you can read the sheets the way you prefer without changing anyone else's. Leave it on "Use this world's setting" to follow whichever layout the GM has chosen for this world. Picking Modern or Classic here sticks across every world you open in this browser, which is the point: it is your preference, not the campaign's.

classicLayoutCharacter.name: Classic Layout: Character Sheets
classicLayoutCharacter.hint: Only applies while the sheets are set to Classic. Ticked, character sheets use the classic layout: tab names across the top, and the stats, debilities, damage, HP, armor, XP and level block pinned above them instead of heading the Moves tab. Untick to keep character sheets on the modern layout while other sheets go classic.

classicLayoutSteading.name: Classic Layout: Steading Sheets
classicLayoutSteading.hint: Only applies while the sheets are set to Classic. Ticked, steading sheets use the classic layout: tab names across the top, the Surplus, Fortunes, Size, Population, Prosperity, Defenses and Debilities band pinned above them, and the homefront moves in a sidebar beside every tab rather than on a tab of their own. Untick to keep steading sheets on the modern layout while other sheets go classic.

classicLayoutNpc.name: Classic Layout: NPC Sheets
classicLayoutNpc.hint: Only applies while the sheets are set to Classic. Ticked, NPC sheets use the classic layout: tab names across the top, with the quick facts pinned above them instead of inside the Details tab. Untick to keep NPC sheets on the modern layout while other sheets go classic.

editPencilRevealDelay.name: Edit Pencil Reveal Delay
editPencilRevealDelay.hint: How long to hover a section (in seconds) before its edit pencil fades in. The pencils stay clickable while still invisible, so you can click one without waiting. Set to 0 to show them instantly.

timeBannerShown.name: Weather and Season Bar
timeBannerShown.hint: Show the weather, the season and the year at the top of the screen. This only affects your own screen.

loveLetterJingle.name: Love Letter Jingle
loveLetterJingle.hint: Ring a short jingle when a love letter arrives for you. The red notice still appears when this is off. This only affects your own screen.

askRollModeEachRoll.name: Ask How to Roll Each Time
askRollModeEachRoll.hint: Ask for Advantage / Normal / Disadvantage in a window before every move or stat roll, starting fresh at Normal each time. Ticked, the Roll Modifier selector is hidden from the character and steading sheets. Unticked, that selector is how you say it, and it stays set until you change it. Hold Shift while clicking a roll to skip the window.

promptRollModifier.name: Prompt for Roll Modifier
promptRollModifier.hint: Ask for a one-off modifier (a held bonus, a GM-granted +1, etc.) before each move or stat roll. Already included when "Ask How to Roll Each Time" is on. Hold Shift while clicking the roll to skip the prompt.

promptDamageModifier.name: Adjust Damage Before Rolling
promptDamageModifier.hint: Ask how to roll damage and what to add to it before each damage roll: advantage or disadvantage on the die, a flat modifier, and extra dice. This is how a bonus your sheet can't know about reaches the dice, like the Storm Markings' +1 damage while you roil with anger. Hold Shift while clicking to skip it for one roll.

openSheetsInEditMode.name: Open Sheets in Edit Mode
openSheetsInEditMode.hint: Open character, steading, monster, and NPC sheets in Edit mode instead of Play mode. The header wrench still switches modes per sheet. NPC sheets you don't own always open in Play mode.

reduceMotion.name: Reduce Motion
reduceMotion.hint: Turn off the decorative animations, transitions, and hover-zoom image popups on Stonetop sheets and dialogs.

restoreWindowsOnReload.name: Restore Open Windows on Reload
restoreWindowsOnReload.hint: Reopen the character, steading, monster, NPC, item, and journal sheets you had open, and the Make Camp window while its camp is still going, at the same position and size, when you reload Foundry. Personal to this browser.

showRollStatChips.name: Show Roll Stat Chips
showRollStatChips.hint: Show labels like +STR and +ANY beside the titles of rollable moves on character and steading sheets. Clicking one rolls the move, the same as clicking its title.

showMoveDescriptionsInChat.name: Show Move Descriptions in Chat
showMoveDescriptionsInChat.hint: Include the full move description in the chat card when rolling a move.

startOfSessionReminders.name: Start-of-Session Reminders
startOfSessionReminders.hint: Post the automatic start-of-session chat reminders, such as the Destined "roll +Omens" nudge. These are public cards the whole table sees. Turn this off to stop them.

deathsDoorPrompt.name: Announce When a Character Is Dying
deathsDoorPrompt.hint: Post a chat card the moment a character is reduced to 0 HP, naming the move they trigger (Death's Door, or their post-death insert's own move). The card never forces the roll; the GM can hold it off until the scene wraps up. On by default.

deathsDoorAutoOpen.name: Open the Dying Character's Move Automatically
deathsDoorAutoOpen.hint: Also open the walkthrough for the move on the dying player's own screen, rather than waiting for them to click the chat card. It opens for the player the character is assigned to and nobody else: not the GM applying the damage, and not the rest of the party. If that player isn't logged in, the GM gets it. Cancelling still leaves the card in chat, so the roll can wait. Requires the setting above.

chatShiftButtons.name: Shift Up/Down Buttons on Roll Cards
chatShiftButtons.hint: Add "Shift Up" and "Shift Down" buttons to move roll cards in chat, letting the GM bump a roll's result to a higher or lower tier. Only the GM sees them. Off by default.

chatWoundPrompt.name: Problematic Wound Reminder on 9- Rolls
chatWoundPrompt.hint: When a character carrying a problematic or permanent wound rolls a 7-9 or a 6-, note the injury on the roll card as something the GM might use to explain the result (Book I, page 243). A reminder only: it never changes the roll. Turn it off if it starts reading as wallpaper, since a wound that never heals will appear on most of that character's cards.

hoverDescriptionSettings.name: On Hover Info
hoverDescriptionSettings.label: Configure
hoverDescriptionSettings.hint: Configure which hover descriptions appear on Stonetop sheets.
hoverDescriptionSettings.title: On Hover Info

hoverDescriptionsEnabled.name: Show On Hover Info
hoverDescriptionsEnabled.hint: Turn off every hover description and hover info panel below at once.

hoverDescriptionsStats.name: Hover Descriptions: Stats
hoverDescriptionsStats.hint: Show stat descriptions when hovering over character sheet stats.

hoverDescriptionsBasicMoves.name: Hover Descriptions: Basic Moves
hoverDescriptionsBasicMoves.hint: Show the move description panel when hovering the Basic Moves list on a character sheet, or the Homefront Moves list on Stonetop's own sheet in the classic layout.

hoverDescriptionsPlaybookMoves.name: Hover Descriptions: Playbook Moves
hoverDescriptionsPlaybookMoves.hint: Show descriptions when hovering over linked move names inside playbook and other move text.

hoverDescriptionsTraits.name: Hover Descriptions: Traits
hoverDescriptionsTraits.hint: Show trait descriptions on follower and companion trait tags.

hoverDescriptionsGearTags.name: Hover Descriptions: Gear Tags
hoverDescriptionsGearTags.hint: Show rules descriptions when hovering over gear tags such as close, piercing, or messy.

hoverDescriptionsMonsterRefs.name: Hover Descriptions: Creature Cross-links
hoverDescriptionsMonsterRefs.hint: On bestiary and stat-block sheets, highlight other creatures' names: hover for their concept, click to open their sheet.

hoverDescriptionsInvocations.name: Hover Descriptions: Invocation Effects
hoverDescriptionsInvocations.hint: On the Lightbearer's Invocations tab and in the level-up picker, explain what an Invocation's Reduced and Empowered effects mean when hovering their labels.

hoverDescriptionsVitals.name: Hover Descriptions: Vitals
hoverDescriptionsVitals.hint: Show what Damage, HP, Armor, XP, and Level mean when hovering those labels on the character sheet.

hoverDescriptionsMonsterTags.name: Hover Descriptions: Monster Tags
hoverDescriptionsMonsterTags.hint: On stat blocks, explain a creature's organization, size, and quality tags (solitary, terrifying, magical, etc.) when hovering them.

hoverDescriptionsSteadingStats.name: Hover Descriptions: Steading Stats
hoverDescriptionsSteadingStats.hint: On Stonetop's sheet, explain Surplus, Fortunes, Prosperity, Defenses, Population, Size, and its Debilities when hovering those labels.

hoverDescriptionsValues.name: Hover Descriptions: Trade Values
hoverDescriptionsValues.hint: In journals and on sheets, explain what a “Value N” trade tier is worth (loot, treasure, gear) when hovering it.

hoverDescriptionsDebilities.name: Hover Descriptions: Debilities
hoverDescriptionsDebilities.hint: In move text and prose, embolden “debility” and explain the three character debilities (Weakened, Dazed, Miserable) when hovering it.

hoverDescriptionsJournalLinks.name: Hover Descriptions: Journal Cross-links
hoverDescriptionsJournalLinks.hint: Show an entry's one-line summary when hovering a link into the Stonetop journals: in journal prose, on stat blocks and NPC sheets, and in the Welcome and Setting Overview windows. Turning this off only removes the hover; links you can and can't open are unchanged.

hoverDescriptionsLoreTerms.name: Hover Descriptions: Lore Terms
hoverDescriptionsLoreTerms.hint: Explain Stonetop's four gods (Danu, Aratis, Helior, Tor) when hovering their names in the Character Introductions prompts and the character creation wizard.

artifactsStartUnidentified.name: Artifacts Arrive Unidentified
artifactsStartUnidentified.hint: Book I, Discoveries pp.430-431. When on, a treasure (from Book II, or one made with Create Item) dropped onto a character sheet arrives with its tags, Value and uses withheld: the player sees only what's obvious at a glance, and has to Know Things or Seek Insight about it to learn more. Off by default, so treasure lands fully described as it always has. Either way you can hide or hand over any single artifact from the mask icon on its gear row.

fightTab.name: Fight tab (replaces the Combat tracker)
fightTab.hint: Stonetop has no initiative. The Combat tab becomes a Fight tab showing who is fighting whom and the group rules that apply, with lines on the map and the extra damage for several attackers filled into damage rolls. Turn it off to get Foundry's Combat tracker back, for example to use an initiative module. Takes a reload.

fightWindowAuto.name: Open the Fight window when a fight starts
fightWindowAuto.hint: When a fight starts on the map you are looking at, the Fight tab opens in a window of its own, and the window closes when the fight ends. If you close it, it stays closed until the next fight. Turn this off to keep fights in the sidebar: the Fight tab's Open in a window button still opens it.
fightWindowAuto.combatName: Open the Combat window when a fight starts
fightWindowAuto.combatHint: When a combat starts on the map you are looking at, Foundry's Combat tracker opens in a window of its own, and the window closes when the combat ends. If you close it, it stays closed until the next combat. Turn this off to keep combat in the sidebar: right-clicking the Combat tab still opens the window.

fightRing.name: Fight buttons when you click a token
fightRing.hint: During a fight, clicking a token you control puts buttons around it: Clash, Let Fly and the damage die for a character, a button for each attack a monster has, and Clash, Let Fly and Order for a follower, which their character rolls for them. Click the token again, or anywhere on the map, to put them away. Right-clicking still opens Foundry's token controls.

newCharacter.confirmContent: This character already has a playbook. Choosing a different one clears everything that came with the old one: its moves (and any moves they taught), special possessions and their gear, background, instinct, lore answers and followers (their actors stay in the sidebar). Name, level, XP, stats, notes, relationships, inventory and arcana stay. Choosing the same playbook again keeps all of it and lets you redo your choices.
newCharacter.changePlaybookContent: Changing {name} from {old} to {new} clears everything that came with {old}: its moves (and any moves they taught), special possessions and their gear, background, instinct, lore answers and followers (their actors stay in the sidebar). Name, level, XP, stats, notes, relationships, inventory and arcana stay.

changeBackground.title: Change Background?
changeBackground.content: Leaving {old} takes away {moves}. What is held there stays on record and comes back if the move does.

backgroundAnswers.title: {background}: {label}
backgroundAnswers.lead: Your Background asks you to choose 1.

seekerMajor.title: {background}: Major Arcanum
seekerMajor.lead: Your Background grants you 1 major arcanum. You've begun to unlock its mysteries: 1 mark goes on the front of its insert.
seekerMajor.pickTask: Pick the □ task you've done for this arcanum.
seekerMajor.stays: {major} stays: it has been played. Your new background grants no second major arcanum.
seekerMajor.owed: Your Background grants you 1 major arcanum, and you haven't chosen it yet.

backgroundNeighbors.title: {background}: Neighbors
backgroundNeighbors.fixed: {names} go on the steading's Neighbors list.

onboarding.savedContent: Your current character creation selections have been saved.

rollCard.writerSilent: The GM's client did not answer in time. It may still go through, so check the card before pressing again.

optionHpLoss.title: Lose {formula} HP?
optionHpLoss.body: {name} rolls {formula} and loses that much HP now. It is HP lost, not damage: armor, Defend and Undying don't reduce it.
optionHpLoss.yes: Roll it and lose the HP
optionHpLoss.notOwner: Only {name}'s owner can lose their HP.

monster.groupHitPointsHint: One member's HP, standing for the whole group. Lose half of it and about half of them are out of the action; at 0 the group is routed.
monster.fightAsGroupHint: Optional (Book I p.416): run the whole group as one combatant. Hit Points becomes the group's pool, damage to it is casualties, and Group size and the two fighting-in-numbers rows appear, counting only those still standing. Leave it off while each token is one creature with its own HP.
monster.resetDefaults: Reset HP & damage die to organization defaults
monster.noMovesSeeNotes: No moves. What this creature does is on the Notes tab.
monster.noWriteUp: Nothing is written up for this creature yet.
monster.noEntry: Not linked to a bestiary entry.
monster.armorBoostRevert: Click to revert Armor to normal
monster.armorBoostNote: Armor boosted to {value} (normally {base}) by “{move}.” Click the move again to revert.

npc.instinctEmpty: No instinct yet. Write one as “to [do something].”
npc.embodimentPlaceholder: A voice, picture, or acting trick (GM note)
npc.relationshipsEmpty: No player characters yet. Each one will appear here at 3 hearts, adjustable per NPC.
npc.relationshipsAllHidden: Nobody ticked yet. Turn on edit mode to choose who appears here, or drop a person on this tab.
npc.giveStats: Give them stats (if they might fight or take orders)
npc.statBlockPlaceholder: @UUID link to a monster stat block, if they fight
npc.threatPlaceholder: @UUID link to a threat write-up, if they're ongoing trouble

bestiary.dangerHeadingPlaceholder: Hazard name (e.g. "Unstable nest"). Use **text** for bold.
bestiary.discoveryHeadingPlaceholder: Discovery heading (e.g. "Strange growths"). Use **text** for bold.
bestiary.noStatBlocks: No stat blocks yet. Create one for the basic creature and any elites or bosses.

relationships.showTooltip: Show this person on the sheet

fight.lineUpHint: Fights already going on are kept as they stand; everyone not fighting anybody yet lines up, heroes on the left and foes on the right, right where everyone already is
fight.openWindowHint: Show this fight in a window you can move and resize, so it stays in view while the sidebar is on Chat
fight.noneGM: No fight on this scene. Start one to see who is fighting whom.
fight.empty: Nobody is in this fight yet.
fight.emptyGM: Nobody is in this fight yet. Add them, or select tokens and use the combat toggle on a token's HUD.
fight.noEngagements: Nobody is engaged. Move a token next to a foe, or target one from range.

dragHint.foes: Drag a foe onto a hero to put it next to them on the map.
dragHint.heroes: Drag a hero onto a foe to put them next to it on the map.

send.noRoom: There is no free space next to {name}.
send.noGM: Only the GM can move {name}, and no GM is connected.
send.refused: The GM's client did not move {name}.

fight.roundsNote: This fight was started in Foundry's tracker, which counts rounds and turns. Stonetop does not take turns.

ring.label: {name} in the fight
ring.swarmAria: Roll damage: all {count} of them on one foe, {formula}
ring.strikeBackAria: Spend 1 of {readiness} Readiness to strike back: {formula}, with disadvantage
ring.strikeBackAriaDangerous: Spend 1 of {readiness} Readiness to strike back: {formula}, rolled straight (Dangerous cancels the disadvantage)
ring.lockEyesAria: Spend 1 of {readiness} Readiness to lock eyes with a foe
ring.lockEyesSaid: {name} locks eyes with {foe}. It rolls damage against {name} and their ward with disadvantage for the rest of the fight.

targets.title: {name}: who does this hit?
targets.hint: Tick more than one only when this attack could hurt them all: an area attack, followers joining in, or the way it is described. Damage is rolled separately against each (Book I, page 414).
targets.several: {move} hit more than one: damage is rolled separately against each, for an attack that could hurt them all (Book I, page 414).

row.ping: Point this out on the map

menu.headcount: How many are in this token

headcount.title: How many are in {name}?
headcount.label: People in this token
headcount.hint: A crew or a warband on one token counts as this many attackers. One person is 1.

end.title: End the fight?
end.body: This takes everyone out of the fight, for every player. Tokens stay where they are.

startWindow.hintStart: Tick everyone in the fight. Anyone not on this map is put near the middle of your view: heroes to the left, foes to the right.
startWindow.hintAdd: Tick who joins the fight. Anyone not on this map is put near the middle of your view.

lists.othersHint: Anyone else on the map. Ticked, they join as foes; move them to the heroes from the tab.

startWindow.noScene: Open a map first: a fight happens on a scene.
startWindow.nobody: There is nobody to add to this fight.
startWindow.imported: Brought {count} from the bestiary into the world's Actors.
startWindow.missed: Couldn't put these in the fight: {names}
startWindow.ungrouped: A linked token can't fight as one group, so these came in as separate tokens: {names}

body.group: {name} is a group monster, found 2 to 5 at a time.
body.horde: {name} is a horde monster, found 6 or more at a time.

scale.tokens: A token for each one, each with its own HP
scale.group: One token for the whole group, fighting as one (Book I p.416, for a fight against another group)

scale.split: {name}: the group is now {count} separate tokens.
scale.splitShort: {name}: only room for {count} of the {wanted} still standing.

seed.alreadyApplied: The damage has already been applied
seed.groupBehind: -{bonus}: group against group, {theirs} outnumber {yours}, so their armor is +{bonus}
seed.bestDie: Roll {name}'s {formula} instead, the hardest-hitting die among you
seed.armorBack: {shown} on the card, {rolled} before their {armor} armor

groupHit.down: one of them goes down, {after} still standing
groupHit.hurt: one of them is hurt ({memberHp} of {hpMax} HP left), {after} still standing
groupHit.unhurt: none of them is hurt, {after} still standing
groupHit.memberDown: {member} takes it and goes down ({oldHp} → 0 HP), {after} still standing
groupHit.moveHint: The first member standing takes a lone blow. Pick another to give it to them instead.

undying.box: Undying: from cutting, stabbing or crushing, so half damage after armor

defend.ask: Who spends Readiness, and on which blow?
defend.noteHalve: {defender} spent Readiness to halve the blow on {ward}.
defend.noteStandIn: {defender} spent Readiness to take the blow for {ward}.
defend.noteParry: {defender} spent Readiness to parry the blow on {ward} and strike back.
defend.noteStandInFree: {defender} took the blow for {ward} (Steadfast Guardian, no Readiness spent).
defend.noteIgnore: {defender} spent Readiness to ignore the blow (A Mighty Rampart).
defend.ignoredLine: ignored it (A Mighty Rampart), no damage
defend.knockedDownChoice: {defender} gets knocked down under the blow on {ward}
defend.noteKnockedDown: {defender} got knocked down, halving the blow (I Get Knocked Down).
defend.safetyFirstOne: {defender} halves it (Safety First, harmful magic: 1 Protection)
defend.safetyFirstChoice: {defender} spends 1 Protection to halve the harmful magic on {ward}
defend.noteSafetyFirst: {defender} spent 1 Protection to halve the harmful magic's damage (Safety First).
defend.secondIntent: {name} parried: also pick 1 option from the Ambush list. The strike back was rolled without the +1d4 damage.
defend.secondIntentTookDie: {name} parried and took +1d4 damage on the strike back: that is their pick from the Ambush list.

undaunted.outnumbered: Undaunted: +1d6 damage, while you are outnumbered
undaunted.bigger: Undaunted: +1d6 damage, facing a foe bigger than you
undaunted.unread: Undaunted: +1d6 damage, if you are outnumbered or facing a foe bigger than you
undaunted.armorBox: Undaunted: +1 armor, if outnumbered or facing a foe bigger than them

leapIn.tooltip: Big Damn Hero: the first time you leap into danger to protect someone, don't roll to Defend. It counts as a 10+. Once per fight.
leapIn.said: {name} leaps into danger to protect someone: no roll to Defend, it counts as a 10+.
leapIn.noFight: No fight on the map to keep count: this is for the first leap into danger in a fight.

toughLove.held: {other} has disadvantage on rolls against you
toughLove.workedOutTooltip: You and {other} have worked it out: their rolls against you are no longer at disadvantage.
toughLove.callTooltip: When you honestly think another PC is in the wrong and call them on it, they have disadvantage on any rolls against you until you two work it out.
toughLove.ask: Which PC do you honestly think is in the wrong?
toughLove.nobody: There is no other player character to call on it.
toughLove.called: {name} calls {other} on it: {other} has disadvantage on any rolls against {name} until they work it out.

rememberMe.label: Something to Remember Me By: +{dice} damage, and you mark them

hungryFlames.label: Hungry Flames: +{dice} damage, and they are engulfed in holy light and flames

nemesis.label: Nemesis: +{dice} damage, against a foe who survived you

payback.label: Payback: +{dice} damage, against a foe who has harmed you or an ally

upAgain.label: But I Get Up Again: +{dice} damage, against whoever knocked you down

bigGame.label: Strike at its weak spot: +{dice} damage (large or huge)

anger.label: Spend 1 Resolve to strike hard: +{dice} damage, forceful

dogWithBone.label: Like a Dog with a Bone: +{dice} damage, against something tainted by chaos

everythingBleeds.label: Everything Bleeds: +{dice} damage, exploiting this unnatural foe's weakness

predator.label: Predator: +{dice} damage, acting on what you learned about your prey

withoutMercy.label: Blood-Soaked Past: +{dice} damage, fighting to kill without mercy or hesitation

heroMoves.takenAtDisadvantage: {move}: the damage against them rolls with disadvantage.

armorGate.barkskin: Barkskin: {armor} armor, while touching the earth
armorGate.candle: A Candle Against the Dark: {armor} armor, wielding a holy light and otherwise unarmed
armorGate.barkskinOrCandle: Barkskin or A Candle Against the Dark: {armor} armor, while touching the earth or wielding a holy light otherwise unarmed (untick only if neither holds)
armorGate.barkskinOrCandleNote: without {armor} armor: neither Barkskin nor A Candle Against the Dark held
armorGate.versus: Not {against}: {armor} armor, which {against} goes straight through

uncanny.label: {name}'s Uncanny Reflexes: roll with disadvantage, for a blow they could dodge or roll with

battlefieldGrace.label: {name}'s Battlefield Grace: roll with disadvantage, while they lead their allies in battle

blotOut.question: Deplete your ammunition before you roll? If you do, pick what the volley buys.
blotOut.area: Area: roll damage separately for each target

battleDancer.title: Battle Dancer: 12+ on +DEX
battleDancer.lead: Instead of picking from the list:
battleDancer.impress: You impress, embarrass or overawe your foes

heroMoves.muscleboundNote: Musclebound: forceful and messy, and more so where it already was.
heroMoves.berserkerHint: Berserker: in your Battle Joy you lash out at anyone nearby, friend and foe alike. Damage is rolled separately for each.
heroMoves.volleyHint: Your volley falls on everyone standing where the arrows land, friend and foe alike. Damage is rolled separately for each.

knockedDown.title: I Get Knocked Down
knockedDown.ask: {name} halves the blow. What does it cost them?
knockedDown.lost: They lose something: footing, grip, their weapon's place in their hand
knockedDown.outOfIt: They are out of it for a moment
knockedDown.note: {name} gets knocked down, halving the blow: {cost}
knockedDown.upAgain: {name} is getting up again: advantage on their next roll against {foe}, and +1d4 on their next blow.

unstoppable.markBox: Unstoppable: mark 1, for damage taken while fighting on at 0 HP
unstoppable.full: Unstoppable: all {max} circles are already marked
unstoppable.insteadAsk: {name} is fighting on at 0 HP and would regain HP (to {hp}). Unstoppable clears one mark instead, which leaves {marks} marked.
unstoppable.insteadNote: {name} would regain HP while fighting, and clears one Unstoppable mark instead ({marks} marked).
unstoppable.regainedNote: {name} regains HP after all (to {hp}), and the Unstoppable mark stays.
unstoppable.hardToKillNotDying: Hard to Kill is rolled at Death's Door, and {name} is not at Death's Door.
unstoppable.fightsOn: Unstoppable: {name} fights on at 0 HP. Roll Death's Door when you stop fighting (the dying card's button, or the sheet).
unstoppable.fightsOnCard: Unstoppable: {name} fights on at 0 HP, and rolls Death's Door when they stop fighting.
unstoppable.stopsFighting: The action stops for {name}, fighting on at 0 HP: time to roll Death's Door.

readiness.ask: {name} holds {count} Readiness and attacks ({move}). Going on the offense loses all of it, but fighting defensively keeps it (p.216). Are they rushing in, or holding their ground?
readiness.lostOffense: {name} goes on the offense ({move}) and loses all held Readiness.
readiness.lostFightOver: The fight is over: {names} let go of their Readiness.
readiness.lostLeftFight: {name} leaves the fight and loses their Readiness.
readiness.lostDown: {name} is down and loses their Readiness.

tip.diligence: Chronicler of Stonetop: {name} spends 1 Diligence ({held} held) to add +1 to this roll.
tip.sanction: Commune with Aratis: acting on Aratis's orders, {name} spends 1 Sanction ({held} held) to add +1 to this roll.
tip.manyHands: Many Hands Make Light Work: {name} jumps in to help. Say how, and ask the GM what else it takes or what it will cost. If you accept, this roll gets +1.
tip.blessing: Piety: in pursuit of a righteous cause, {name} spends their Blessing from worship to Helior to add +1 to this roll.

rollBoosts.refused: The +1 was not added: it has already been used on this roll, the track is empty, or no GM is here to record it.

piety.title: Who worshipped with you?
piety.hint: Each faithful PC who took part in the worship holds 1 Blessing, to spend for +1 on a roll of their own. Close this window if nobody else did.
piety.missed: No GM is online to give {names} a Blessing. Use Piety again once one is.
